blocks.h2: What to Do if a Pipe Bursts

steps.body: Usually in the basement near the meter.
If you can reach the breaker safely.

blocks.h2: How to Tell a Pipe Has Burst in a Geneva Home

bullets: In older homes, water trapped behind plaster pushes it out or stains it brown.

tiles.h3: Water Dripping From a Light Fixture
bullets: Water follows wiring and framing. Shut off the water and the breaker for that circuit.
Water is escaping before it gets to the faucet.
Every fixture is off, and the meter keeps turning.

blocks.h2: Signs a Pipe Is Frozen, Not Yet Burst

tiles.h3: A Faucet on an Outside Wall Is Dry
tiles.body: Kitchen sinks on exterior walls are the classic first freeze.
The supply line to it may be frozen in the wall.

tiles.h3: Frost Where the Pipe Enters the House
tiles.body: The water service coming through a cold foundation wall can freeze in a deep cold snap.

blocks.h2: Where Pipes Freeze in Geneva Homes
blocks.intro: Fox Valley winters bring stretches well below freezing, and older homes have more weak spots.

items.body: Homes in the Central Geneva Historic District were built long before modern insulation. Pipes running up exterior walls are exposed to cold air all winter.
Plumbing added to an old house often runs through the coldest spaces, like an enclosed porch or a north wall.
Cold seeps through old stone foundations, and pipes along the top of the basement wall feel it first.

items.h3: Rooms Over Garages in Newer Homes
items.body: West side homes built after 1990 often have a bathroom over an attached garage, with pipes in a cold floor.

blocks.h2: Burst Pipe Questions From Geneva Homeowners

items.q: How do I thaw a frozen pipe safely?
items.preview: Open the faucet and warm the pipe slowly. No flames.
items.answer: Open the faucet, then warm the pipe with a hair dryer or space heater, starting near the faucet. Never use a torch. If you can't reach it, call us.

items.q: How do I protect pipes in an old house?
items.preview: Keep the heat up, open cabinets and drip faucets in a deep freeze.
items.answer: Keep the heat at 55 degrees or higher, open cabinet doors on exterior walls, let faucets drip on the coldest nights and seal drafts near pipes. We can insulate or reroute problem lines.

items.q: Why did my pipe leak after the cold snap?
items.answer: The pipe split while frozen and only leaked once it thawed.

items.q: Should I replace my outdoor spigot?
items.preview: A freeze-resistant spigot prevents a common burst.
items.answer: Yes, if it's an older style. A freeze-resistant spigot closes the water off inside the heated part of the wall.
